extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in the French newspaper Le Monde (Wikipedia readership)
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic (Wikipedia) article describing Le Monde: its publication practices, sections, online services, governance, finances, editorial independence arrangements, and criticisms/controversies. The page documents procedural rules and standards the paper follows or is judged by.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication dating and closing time (bouclage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Le Monde is dated the day after its day of printing (daté du lendemain). The editorial 'bouclage' is done at 10:30 in the morning, allowing inclusion of overnight or early-morning information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: editions printed on a given day bear the next day's date; the 10:30 cut-off lets the paper integrate late-breaking items that other papers (which close overnight) cannot. Example: an edition leaving press Friday 1st is dated Saturday 2nd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper section structure and page-allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical daily découpage with defined pages and functions: La une (lead tribune, central editorial, drawing, brief items), Page two (daily press cartoon), Page three (in-depth investigation), Planète (1–2 pages environment), International/International & Europe (4–5 pages), France (3–4 pages, mainly politics), Économie (2–3 pages), Décryptages (3–4 pages for tribunes/debates/investigations), Culture (2–3 pages; Wednesday = cinema), & Vous (practical life), Carnet (obituaries, announcements), last page (readers' letters and a guest billet d'humeur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The structure is flexible: the newsroom may allocate more pages to a theme in response to major events (e.g., Planète grew for the March 2011 Japan earthquake). This sectioning implies editorial expectations for content type and depth per page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of counter-investigations (contre-enquête)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issue of Le Monde 'proposes a contre-enquête' which may concern any rubric of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial practice: include counter-investigations to revisit or challenge reporting within the paper; indicates a formal commitment to investigative follow-up across sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online access and archive policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all textual content on lemonde.fr is accessible free each day in early afternoon. Articles younger than three days are also freely accessible but without the journal's iconographic and infographic material. Archive access: non-subscribers have limited free consultation (25 archive articles per month); full archives and multimedia require paid subscription (paid section available since April 2002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for readers and producers: the site balances free access to recent journalism with paywalled archival/multimedia content; subscription offerings explicitly include agency dispatches and databases. NOTE: the paper discontinued PDF delivery for subscribers in 2021 citing fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Les Décodeurs - fact-checking mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Les Décodeurs (created 10 March 2014) sets itself the objective 'de vérifier les informations' given on varied themes in the media and on Internet (fact-checking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operates as a dedicated team (~10 journalists) to check claims; positioned to 'control the veracity of statements of politicians' and similar public claims. The section has been both praised for filling a fact-checking role and critiqued for impartiality/limitations (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Décodex - source verification tool purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Décodex is presented as 'un outil de vérification de l'information' using a database of hundreds of sites (mainly French, also English/German/US) to help distinguish reliable sources from misleading, conspiratorial or strongly biased sites. Presented as intended for teachers (and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: browser extension and website search to classify media outlets; at launch described in press as a step toward automated checking (even reference to a 'robot Facebook'). Criticisms and limits (e.g., favoring professional media, potential limited usefulness beyond convinced readers) are documented elsewhere in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence — director appointment voting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the paper's official statutes, the appointment ('nomination') of the director of the newsroom must be voted by at least 60% of the newsroom's journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This internal rule is presented as a device to avoid shareholder pressure on journalists; it is a formal, statutory safeguard for editorial appointment processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pôle d'indépendance — statute protection (golden share)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2017 the Pôle d’indépendance du Monde obtained a 'golden share' in modified statutes that protects its statutory rights regardless of its share of capital; minority shareholders thus have the power to block decisions of majority shareholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism: statutory blocking power intended to secure editorial independence from capital shifts. The article notes this as an originality to protect against pressures of shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an inalienable endowment fund for shareholding
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2020 Xavier Niel placed all his shares in a special 'fonds de dotation' which is legally inalienable (incessible) intended to protect independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records expert concerns (Julia Cagé) about governance gaps: although legally inalienable, the fund remains under Niel's control, and growing numbers of Niel's direct employees on the supervisory board raise independence questions. This illustrates that structural devices must be complemented by governance transparency and limits on board composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of finances and revenue model
rubrics_metrics.description: The Groupe Le Monde publishes its financial documents (balance sheet, income statement) annually to readers. Subscription is currently the paper's principal revenue source; the group also receives state press aids and specific amounts are reported (e.g., historic subsidy figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation: public disclosure of financials as a transparency practice. The entry lists circulation and revenue indicators to inform readers about commercial independence and financial health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and correction practices exemplified by mediator guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediator reflections and past controversies emphasize avoiding publication of unverified extracts of investigation records, verifying testimony, and waiting to allow subjects to respond before publishing allegations. Example: in the Dominique Baudis affair the mediator noted errors including publication of unverified extracts and stressed practices like waiting for the subject to express and react in the paper's columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard implied: cross-check sources, avoid reproducing non-recouped (not corroborated) testimonies or extracts of judicial files without verification; seek subject response and report counter-attacks; quickly correct or withdraw erroneous material (example: erroneous announcement of Bernard Tapie's death was rapidly removed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poll reporting standards — disclose sample limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission des sondages criticized Le Monde for headlining a result about 18–24-year-olds without indicating that the 18–24 subsample contained fewer than 200 people (small under-sample), i.e., not signalling the small sub-sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied rule: when reporting poll results, explicitly state sample sizes, sub-sample sizes and limitations so readers can judge statistical reliability; failure to do so is a recognized error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest procedures and ethics oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The article records a January 2024 controversy (nomination of Rayan Nezzar) and notes that the Society of Editors referred the matter to the group's ethics committee to evaluate precautions taken by management regarding conflict-of-interest risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial expectation: appoint ethics committees / procedures to evaluate and manage conflicts of interest; transparency about affiliations and prior relationships is required to preserve trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and funding must respect editorial integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Les Décodeurs is financed in part by Facebook; the management asserts the partnership allowed team growth 'en respectant l'intégrité du contenu' (respecting content integrity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for evaluating funding/partnerships: they must not compromise editorial independence or content integrity—this is an explicit claim and a standard against which such arrangements are judged. The article also documents debate/concern about such partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking tool critique — impartiality and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques of Les Décodeurs/Décodex stress difficulties in being 'impartial and transparent' and question usefulness beyond already-convinced readers; critics worry the system privileges professional media and that Le Monde may be 'judge and party'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a fact-checking initiative, consider: transparency of criteria, impartiality (not being 'judge and party'), potential biases toward mainstream/professional outlets, and whether the tool aids undecided readers versus only reinforcing existing beliefs.
